title: A long `elseif` chain overflows the compiler's stack, and a long `else if` chain is refused as too deep.
text: `finish_if` (`crates/nvs-syntax/src/parser/stmt.rs:403`) calls itself for every `elseif` without going through `parse_statement`'s `guarded`, so the chain is never counted against `MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH` (96, `parser/mod.rs:194`) and builds an `If` nested in `else_` once per arm. A probe on the debug `nvs check` crashed with `has overflowed its stack` (exit 253) at 300 `elseif` arms and passed at 200. The same chain spelled `else if` is guarded, and is refused with `E0108` already at 90 arms. Both are defects: a long `if`/`elseif` chain is ordinary PHP, and its cost should be linear with no depth at all. The root fix represents the chain as one statement with a list of arms (or lowers it iteratively), so neither spelling nests and every later walk over it is a loop. Ladder: `compiler/elseif.nvs`, n arms from 64 upward, `compile` kind; it should be flat per arm and never crash.
